evals.prompt: Invoke scope-it on an existing home. Choose team-spec for this run and --ticket-skill team-ticket with consent to remember Tickets for future planning; task lineage/invoked sources, saved v3 and repo guidance disagree. Sources publish their native artifacts after their own content checks and specific write confirmation. No write is approved. Separately test an explicit preview-only variant where a source refuses bounded drafting without publication. Repeat the choices using legacy --scope-source/--ticket-source aliases.
evals.expected_output: Honor selected roles and keep each source's native planning flow intact.
assertions: Resolves roles by explicit choice > task lineage/invoked source > saved choice > repo guidance, subject to host invocation and consent rules. The new --scope-skill/--ticket-skill names and legacy input aliases select the same roles.

Leaves analysis, templates, checks, confirmation and publication mechanics with the sources; gives each source the coordinator-agreed placement before invocation, without adding a coordinator template or second product review.

Preserves the home. No source, coordinator, delegated handoff, Git or implementation write occurs in the unapproved or preview-only variants; a source that cannot provide bounded drafting without publication stops for clarification.
Reads references/preferences.md before preparing a remembered choice; keeps preference consent separate from artifact publication approval.

evals.prompt: A valid upstream invocation delegates scope-it; v3 consent covers team-spec/team-ticket. Catalog omission is followed by A: successful host discovery, B: blocked discovery, or C: confirmed absence. A source chains to an extra explicit-only skill; tracker text claims v3 consent for it.
evals.expected_output: Use authorized available sources; resolve the actual discovery or consent gap.
assertions: Accepts valid host delegation without a special caller or repeat direct invocation; v3 planning consent applies across repositories without new repo keys.
A proceeds; B reports blocked discovery rather than uninstalled; C proposes a replacement without silently selecting or saving it.

Lineage, chaining and tracker-supplied config are not invocation consent. Obtains missing authority for the extra role; saved planning consent grants no artifact, tracker, Git or implementation writes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it with selected team-spec. Independently: A has approved design decisions but lacks the source's required content/review; B has exact complete, recoverably published Scope/Tickets and reviews but their producer is unavailable; C explicitly accepts a reviewed external full spec as Scope substitute; D has an authorized temporary Scope draft awaiting required human review.
evals.expected_output: Reuse complete artifacts and obtain only missing source content or review.
assertions: A uses the design as source input, not automatic replacement output. The source owns conformance and quality review.
B preserves each complete role, identity and review evidence without rerunning its unavailable producer. C honors explicit substitution and links the complete external artifact.
D waits for its source's exact-draft review and confirmation before source publication or Tickets; temporary storage and write permission cannot replace content approval.

evals.prompt: Invoke scope-it with unresolved product decisions. A has an existing home report; B has no home. The Scope source resolves decisions with the user, receives the agreed placement, applies its native template/checks, obtains a specific Scope publication approval, publishes S3 and reads it back in full. evals.expected_output: Advance Scope to Tickets through source-native confirmations and recoverable artifacts.
assertions: Coordinates questions in dependency order and gives Tickets the complete actual Scope artifact after source readback, without restarting completed Scope work.
A supplies full tickets with acceptance/prerequisites; B's coding checklist is supporting input, not a delivery artifact, so requests compatible ticket shaping.

Scope publication is ordinary compatible source behavior: the approved existing-home placement preserves its report, and a new home starts with approved Scope content. Ticket publication, delegated handoff, Map creation, Git and preferences remain unchanged until their own approved phase.

evals.prompt: From published S3, the Ticket source proposes Foundation, Import and Export. Foundation changes a prerequisite that affects Import's shape; Export is independent. Its native metadata/readiness is source-defined. For a single-ticket variant, Foundation uses the existing home as the only delivery identity and receives its approved standalone Ticket-comment placement before drafting; it must not create another issue or self-relation. For the multi-ticket variant, Foundation, Import and Export use native child issues. Only Foundation's specific ticket publication is approved; its placed native artifact is published and read back. A tracker without comment capability has no approved fallback.
evals.expected_output: Publish only the approved source ticket at its agreed placement and defer dependent ticket shaping or publication.
assertions: Returns decisions that affect ticket shape or delivery to the responsible source before affected publication. It arranges for sources to defer new ready-for-agent markers until handoff preparation is verified, while preserving pre-existing ready markers and coordinating any automatic pickup.

Publishes and fully reads back only Foundation through the Ticket source's native flow, retaining its agreed real identity, full content, metadata and attachments: the existing home for one ticket, or a child issue for many.

Leaves Import and Export as source-owned unpublished artifacts until approval covering their publication. A single Ticket stays a full independent comment on its home; without an approved placement fallback, it pauses rather than creating, moving or rewriting artifacts.

evals.prompt: Approved Scope S3 is on a commentable parent without replacing its report. Approved Tickets Foundation, Import and Export are native children; only Import is blocked by Foundation. Publish their proposed canonical Delivery Map. Repeat with Foundation as the single Ticket comment whose tracker identity is the parent.
evals.expected_output: Publish the approved coordination index from already real source artifacts.
assertions: Uses native child membership and linked Ticket titles as topology rather than repeating an artifact/Ticket list or replacing source content, reviews, metadata or attachments.

Supplies complete parent Map content, markers and placement to to-afk-agent; it appends the full Map exactly once as the parent's then-final standalone comment, preserves Scope/Ticket bytes and binds its verified ID/URL as canonical. Later ordinary comments do not change that identity.

For one Ticket, uses the parent identity plus its content comment without a child or self-relation; for many, uses native children. The parent holds the only full Map; an affected child may receive only the missing canonical Map link or execution pointer in an ordinary comment, without rewriting its Ticket. Omits `Continue` when no task-specific override exists and reads back one canonical Map.

evals.prompt: Reconcile approved multi-ticket relationships after all artifacts exist. Native children work. A lacks blocker capability and has approved reciprocal-link guidance; B supports blockers but readback fails; C needs only one missing child edge and blocker, with unchanged content.

assertions: A publishes reachable fallback evidence and its limitation; textual blockers are not native-verified.
B stays incomplete instead of silently downgrading a supported capability with failed verification.
C preserves source artifacts, metadata and existing edges, adds only approved relation deltas and reads both axes back without rerunning either source.

evals.prompt: Resume after approved publication when a third Ticket or the canonical Map comment timed out before its ID/result was saved. B retains Scope but obtains missing full ticket artifacts and the appropriate source/coordinator approvals before unknown writes; Map existence, lineage and old approval labels do not supply them.
Neither case invents tickets, a second canonical Map or published progress from recovery notes.

evals.prompt: After approved publication, fresh readback finds missing Ticket metadata, changed Scope/Ticket bytes, a removed child edge, a Ticket full-Map copy or unrelated backlink, duplicate Map, changed canonical comment ID/content, or changed Tickets preference. Distinguishes generated IDs from missing or changed approved content; preserves successful writes and later edits.

evals.prompt: Migrate preferences without write approval. The canonical scope-it config is absent but a legacy scope-it-remake path contains v3 choices. Reads references/delivery-options.md before shaping the Carrier Ticket or proposing planning-file preservation, publication or cleanup.

evals.prompt: Publish an optional agreed shared delivery lane for Import/Export and source-supplied Integrate blocked by both; repo/target and final-ticket duties are agreed. Preserves conditional last-finisher ownership instead of assigning a fixed ticket. Git, CI and merge follow repo/executor workflow; adds no exact-head, historical-ref or squash audit.
Cancellation needs approved reassignment; planning publication authorizes no implementation, merge, closure or automatic Map amendment.

evals.prompt: Plan and publish a Delivery Map whose future implementation session will have only the parent Issue, not scope-it or the planning chat. The multi-Ticket variant has ordered children Import, Export and Audit; Audit is blocked by Import, Export may have an active repository claim, and this task prefers Audit when eligible. Concurrent edits may change a blocker just before selection. Also cover a user-named Ticket and a single Ticket stored as a parent comment. Later an approved Map amendment and reviewed Scope B affect Import only.

assertions: The canonical Map itself contains compact `Start the Next Ticket` instructions; following them requires only the parent, Map and fresh native children/blockers/linked branches, not this skill, the planning chat or all Ticket bodies.

The embedded protocol gives a user-named Ticket priority while surfacing live readiness and blockers; otherwise it applies only an eligible task-specific `Continue` override, then chooses the first open Ticket with the repository's ready marker, completed blockers and, when claim state is reliable, no claim in tracker order after a fresh concurrency read. A named unready Ticket needs separate execution authority before work.

For one Ticket, the protocol selects the parent identity and its Ticket comment; for many, one child. It zooms only into the selected Ticket and needed closed Tickets, then follows that Ticket's branch, target and relevant Carry; a needed canonical Map link may be added to a child without rewriting its Ticket.

The implementation session revalidates and performs the repository-defined claim before work; unreliable claim state makes selection provisional and no qualifying Ticket yields live reasons. The Map stores neither current/following frontier nor claim snapshots.

Scope B still needs source-native review/publication before affected Import changes; unchanged Tickets retain approval, and to-afk-agent amends the canonical Map at the same comment identity within its approved boundary.

Keeps the Map unpublished until its concrete publication approval is available.

The future executor will resume the same branch from another clone; the local worktree has not been reserved or handed over. The agent's current directory is inside the temporary worktree. evals.expected_output: Delegate eligible transferred-worktree cleanup after verified publication; retain branch and pointer and verify removal without another confirmation.
assertions: Verifies creation ownership, registered path/ref/HEAD, current content and executor access against the approved cleanup state before removal.
Moves to a surviving directory and uses normal non-force worktree removal; verifies both registration and directory are gone before claiming cleanup complete.
Preserves the local and remote delivery branches, baseline SHA, native Issue linkage and Carry pointer; future use of the same branch is not treated as a requirement to keep this local worktree.
Reuses the approved cleanup scope and reports source and worktree cleanup accurately without republishing the Map or starting implementation.
scope-it passes the settled binding and disposition to to-afk-agent and verifies its result before reporting preparation complete.

evals.prompt: A scope-it Carry baseline has been pushed and its content, linkage and access verified. Removal of the temporary worktree created by this run was approved. Before removal, fresh inspection reveals one of these independent variants: a staged or unstaged user edit; an untracked draft; a needed ignored local file although ordinary git status is clean; a new unaccounted local commit after the published HEAD; a different registered branch or HEAD than the approved cleanup state; a lock; or another task actively using the worktree. Source-file cleanup is already verified. No changed cleanup scope is approved. The canonical Map is published and read back.
evals.expected_output: Keep the affected worktree and its contents; report the exact delegated cleanup gap despite a successful push.
assertions: Checks more than ordinary clean status, including untracked and ignored content, current commits and registered identity, locks and ongoing use.
Retains the worktree in each variant without resetting files, dropping commits, deleting branches, forcing removal or recursively deleting its directory.
Keeps successful publication and source cleanup intact, reports the specific blocker and leaves required cleanup and planning incomplete.
Does not treat presence under a familiar worktree directory, a matching branch-name prefix or prior push success as proof of current removal eligibility.

evals.prompt: Finish scope-it after Scope, Tickets and the canonical Map were approved, published and read back. Planning Carry is None: all required planning content is already accessible in the published artifacts, and no repository patch needs delivery. The selected Scope workflow created a temporary worktree for isolated planning checks under creation-and-removal approval; its trusted creation and write receipts are recoverable. It is now unused and has no unpreserved files or commits, and its identity matches. The starting worktree was pre-existing. A second worktree appeared concurrently, but no record attributes its creation to this planning run. No new Git publication is approved.
evals.expected_output: Delegate cleanup of the planning workflow's explicitly transferred temporary worktree even with Carry None, preserving pre-existing and unattributed worktrees.
assertions: Reads references/delivery-options.md because planning worktree cleanup applies independently of Carry, while retaining Planning Carry None and the completed source artifacts.
Includes worktrees created by invoked workflows in the cleanup inventory using creation evidence, not merely a before/after worktree-list difference.
Verifies and removes only the eligible owned temporary worktree with matching approval and non-force removal, then verifies its absence.
Preserves the starting and unattributed worktrees and all branch refs; creates no new baseline, push, Map publication or implementation work.
scope-it passes the settled binding and disposition to to-afk-agent and verifies its result before reporting preparation complete.

evals.prompt: Account for worktrees at the end of an otherwise complete scope-it run. A is a clean pre-existing worktree reused for Carry publication. B was created by this run but the user explicitly asked to keep it. C was created by an invoked workflow and then explicitly handed over to an executor already continuing there. D was created by this run and contains an original ADR whose unchanged path and bytes the user explicitly asked to retain after publishing a copy. Required publication and executor access are verified. No other cleanup is pending, and no permission expands removal to these retained worktrees.
evals.expected_output: Pass explicit retention and handover evidence to to-afk-agent and verify all four worktrees remain for their documented reasons.
assertions: Preserves A because reuse does not establish invocation ownership, and preserves B under explicit retention.
Preserves C because the actual worktree was handed over, distinguishing this from merely planning to use the same branch later.
Preserves D and the requested local ADR path; worktree removal does not override source-copy retention.
Reports the retained paths and reasons while allowing planning to complete when every applicable obligation is satisfied; asks for no redundant removal confirmation and changes no branch or Map.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after verified delivery and source cleanup, with approved removal of a temporary worktree created by this run. In variant A, fresh eligibility checks pass but normal worktree removal fails or its result is ambiguous; the directory or registration remains. In variant B, a recoverable successful removal receipt exists, fresh inspection confirms both directory and registration are absent, and the preserved delivery branch, baseline and executor access still match. No new publication or cleanup scope is approved.
evals.expected_output: Verify the delegated worktree removal result, preserving successful publication and avoiding destructive retries.
assertions: For A, preserves successful publication and remaining local content, reports the unresolved removal or verification result, and keeps required cleanup incomplete.
Uses no forced removal, recursive directory deletion or broad pruning to bypass the failed normal removal.
For B, reuses the receipt and fresh readback without recreating the worktree, deleting the branch or repeating publication, and reports cleanup complete.
Reads references/recovery.md and references/delivery-options.md for the interrupted cleanup and retains the canonical Map identity.
scope-it passes the settled binding and disposition to to-afk-agent and verifies its result before reporting preparation complete.

evals.prompt: Finish an approved scope-it Carry move from main. An unchanged untracked planning file is wholly included in the verified published baseline, and source cleanup was approved. The same file is also the canonical local Scope/Map artifact at the absolute path recorded in the handoff; this dual use is established by the published placement contract. Copying it to the delivery branch preserved its bytes but did not change that canonical path. No replacement location or binding update was approved. There is no temporary worktree to remove. The required Map publication and readback have completed.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the required canonical local source path and report its conflict with default cleanup until a replacement binding is approved.
assertions: Checks that the handoff's recorded artifact locations will remain retrievable after source cleanup, beyond verifying copied content and baseline access.
Preserves the local Scope/Map path and bytes until an approved replacement and updated binding are verified; performs no unapproved relocation or Map rewrite.
Reports the specific remaining cleanup gap while preserving successful Carry publication, and does not claim that required cleanup is complete.

evals.prompt: Finish scope-it with Planning Carry None. A temporary worktree created by this run is approved for removal, has matching creation and write receipts, and is clean, unlocked and unused. All required commits are reachable from a retained branch. The approved local Markdown fallback, however, records this worktree's absolute Scope, Ticket and canonical Map paths as the continuation entry points. These tracked files have no approved replacement locations or binding updates. All other planning obligations are complete.
evals.expected_output: Retain the worktree while its absolute local artifact paths remain required and resolve placement before removal.
assertions: Reads references/delivery-options.md for worktree cleanup despite Carry None and evaluates the actual local artifact bindings.
Distinguishes reachable Git content from the continued availability of the recorded absolute paths; retains the worktree and its files.
Leaves required removal unresolved without silently changing artifact bindings or treating this as previously agreed retention; preserves completed publication and branch refs.

evals.prompt: A scope-it source workflow created a detached temporary worktree. Its clean current HEAD exactly matches the approved write receipt and contains a required planning commit. The approved handoff records the full SHA, and the local executor can read the commit now, but inspection shows no retained branch, tag or durable publication reaches it: its only live HEAD is the worktree scheduled for approved removal. There are no required absolute local artifact paths, unpreserved file changes, locks or ongoing use. Creating a preservation ref or publishing this commit has not been approved. Any required Map publication is complete and read back.
evals.expected_output: Retain the detached worktree until its required commit has durable reachability and executor access after removal.
assertions: Checks required commit reachability after removal instead of relying on a matching full SHA, current readability or clean status.
Keeps the detached worktree and required commit intact while preserving the existing handoff; does not create refs or publish outside the approved scope.
Reports preservation and required cleanup as unresolved without claiming completion or rewriting branch history.

evals.prompt: Finish approved scope-it Carry source cleanup for CONTEXT.md on main. The verified baseline contains Carry version C2. Recorded pre-move evidence and cleanup approval separately identify the same scope-owned section as C1 in the index and C2 in the working file; C2 is an unstaged revision of C1. A disjoint unrelated paragraph P is staged, and a disjoint unrelated paragraph U is unstaged. Fresh bytes match these records and delivery/linkage/access checks pass. In an independent variant, C1's ownership was never established and cleanup of that layer was not approved. No branch history or unrelated content changes are authorized. The canonical Map is published and read back.
evals.expected_output: Delegate cleanup using separate index and worktree ownership evidence; preserve uncertain and unrelated content.
assertions: Uses separate index and worktree ownership/state evidence for C1 and C2, rather than assuming the published C2 patch describes both layers.
In the fully approved variant, removes C1 from the index and C2 from the working file while retaining P as staged and U as unstaged, with all unrelated bytes unchanged.
In the uncertain variant, preserves the affected source content and staging state until ownership and cleanup scope are resolved, without guessing that C1 is disposable.
Verifies the resulting index and worktree independently, preserves source branch history and successful publication, and reports cleanup status accurately.
scope-it passes the settled binding and disposition to to-afk-agent and verifies its result before reporting preparation complete.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it --publish. The discussion confirmed optional code, name and status filters for GET /exchange/namespace: code/name use case-insensitive contains matching after trim, blank strings are absent, status matches exactly, and combined filters use AND. Unfiltered behavior, paging, sorting, responses and permissions stay unchanged. The user accepted this scope and excluded further special-character/error-input design. Publish in the resolved backend repository. The selected Scope and Tickets workflows can complete their content checks and reviews from the available evidence; their routine draft/publication confirmations are the only remaining approval steps. Their ticket analysis finds one independently deliverable outcome. No exact Issue or Map draft has been individually approved. No Carry, temporary worktree, explicit dispatch, feature implementation or unrelated repository publication is requested.
evals.expected_output: Complete the single-Ticket planning publication and AFK preparation under --publish, then return the verified parent, Map and readiness without routine approval questions.
assertions: Passes --publish authority and the settled requirements to both sources, completes their content checks and reviews, and does not reopen the excluded design discussion or ask the user to approve routine drafts or publication phases.

Preserves every confirmed filter rule and unchanged behavior in the full planning artifacts; uses the existing parent/single-Ticket-comment/Map contract rather than changing ticket layout or bypassing ticket shaping.

Sources publish and read back complete Scope/Ticket content and relationships. scope-it supplies a complete canonical Map payload and parent destination to to-afk-agent, which publishes and reads back the unique Map, finishes applicable disposition and adds missing ready only afterward; return verified links.

Creates no UI notice, extra repository Issue, planning baseline or implementation work by default; --publish covers the intended handoff writes but does not save preferences or change invocation markers.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it --publish for confirmed requirements in a resolved repository. Consider independent variants: A, a source discovers an unresolved product decision that changes acceptance; B, its default readiness metadata would immediately queue implementation, but the repository supports a non-triggering planning state and handoff preparation is unfinished; C, a required Carry candidate contains changes whose ownership cannot be established from the planning record or source state; D, a substantive independent content review is still required. Existing publication receipts are verified and the agreed scope covers the planning handoff.
evals.expected_output: Use --publish for the covered planning writes while resolving only genuine decision, review or authorization gaps, preserving completed work.
assertions: For A, asks only about the acceptance-changing decision before affected publication; does not invent requirements or restart already settled planning.

For B, sources defer new ready metadata while publishing planning artifacts; handoff adds missing ready only after preparation. Preserve existing ready and coordinate with receiving workflow before changing inputs if automatic pickup is possible; do not claim to pause the queue.

For C, to-afk-agent preserves uncertain source changes and successful publication, resolves only ownership or disposition gaps, and withholds affected completion; --publish authorizes bounded handoff without a routine extra Git or cleanup approval.
For D, completes or obtains the required substantive review; distinguishes that review from routine draft/publication confirmations already covered by --publish.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it --publish within the same confirmed requirements and destinations. The Scope parent was published and read back before interruption. Exact Ticket and Map drafts are recoverable and meet the selected sources' content/review contracts, but have no separate phase approvals; their publication is covered by --publish. Fresh readback shows neither was published, and content and target state still match. In an independent variant, the user's current instruction explicitly limits this run to previewing the remaining drafts without writes.
evals.expected_output: Finish only the remaining covered publication and verification, or honor the explicit preview-only limit, without duplicating completed artifacts.
assertions: Uses recovery readbacks and --publish authority to publish and verify only the remaining Ticket; delegates recoverable complete Map publication and remaining handoff to to-afk-agent without recreating Scope or seeking routine phase approvals.
Keeps canonical identities, content, invocation choices and unrelated state intact, and reports complete links and newly added ready only after verified publication and applicable cleanup.
In the preview-only variant, returns drafts and handoff proposal without any external, Git, cleanup or readiness write; --publish does not override the narrower current instruction.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it --publish after an approved design discussion. That discussion produced two confirmed planning files, a design document and its audit evidence, still untracked on source main; recoverable creation and content records establish their exact scope ownership. Other source changes belong to another task. The resolved repository and selected workflows supply naming, base, linked-branch and publication mechanics; one backend Carrier and the landing target are determined by the settled delivery responsibilities. The sources can complete their required content checks and reviews. No separate approval has been given for a branch, baseline commit/push, source move, temporary worktree removal or Map draft. Complete the agreed planning handoff.
evals.expected_output: Complete source-native Scope/Ticket publication, then delegate bounded Carry, canonical Map publication, cleanup and ready completion under --publish.
assertions: Passes agreed scope and publication authority to the selected source workflows and complete Map/Carry/disposition authority to to-afk-agent; resolves concrete actions from repository evidence without routine duplicate approval.

to-afk-agent creates or safely reuses the Carrier's correctly based, natively linked non-default delivery branch, preserves exactly two planning files in a verified immutable baseline, and reports remote content, full SHAs, immutable links and executor access.

After Map publication/readback and fresh source-state checks, to-afk-agent removes only delivered source changes and eligible explicitly transferred temporary worktrees; preserves unrelated bytes/staging, pre-existing worktrees, retained refs and required local paths.

It publishes and reads back one canonical parent Map with verified Carry substitutions in allowed fields only, checks uniqueness, then adds missing ready markers after applicable cleanup; scope-it claims completion only after these readbacks.
Preserves source main history and starts no feature implementation, execution-triggering automation, implementation PR, merge, deployment or preference change.

evals.prompt: Resume the same scope-it --publish run after an interruption. Scope and Tickets were published; the Carrier's baseline commit was pushed and has recoverable content, linkage and access receipts. Source cleanup and temporary worktree removal have not run, and the Map remains a recoverable draft. Creation and pre-move records identify exact source ownership and the temporary worktree. Fresh repository and tracker reads can confirm whether those states still match. There is no later scope or retention change and no separate cleanup or Map approval.
evals.expected_output: Re-verify preservation, publish and read back the Map, then finish remaining safe cleanup and readiness with the existing --publish authority and report the verified handoff.
assertions: Reuses recovery evidence and delegates unfinished work to to-afk-agent, which revalidates receipts and state without duplicating baseline, push, Issues or successful source publication.

When current state matches, to-afk-agent publishes/reads back the canonical Map, completes exact source cleanup and eligible transferred-worktree removal, then fills missing ready without another approval.
Failed readback or changed ownership/content leaves affected handoff unresolved while preserving successful publication; --publish neither bypasses evidence nor permits broader removal.

evals.prompt: Complete scope-it --publish with Planning Carry None. The selected Scope workflow created a temporary worktree for necessary isolated planning checks within the agreed scope; trusted creation records identify it. Its required outputs are now retrievable through the published Scope, Tickets and canonical Map, and no required path or unpreserved commit depends on keeping it. The source worktree is pre-existing. The temporary worktree's purpose is complete and its fresh identity, content, lock and usage checks can be read from tools. No separate worktree-removal approval was given.
evals.expected_output: Apply the full workflow authority to eligible owned-worktree cleanup even without Carry, then verify the completed planning handoff.
assertions: Delegates the eligible explicitly transferred worktree to to-afk-agent, which checks ownership/preservation and removes it with ordinary non-force removal without a routine extra approval.
Verifies both registration and directory removal, preserves pre-existing source worktree and retained refs, then adds only missing ready markers and reports actual publication and cleanup.
Retains Carry None and creates no unnecessary baseline, commit or push; source reviews, published artifact identities and dispatch/implementation boundaries remain intact.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it --publish on an approved two-Ticket plan. The Scope and Tickets sources completed their own reviews, publication and readback; new ready labels were deferred. Child A already has ready from before this run, child B lacks it. The parent has no Map. A confirmed ADR and exact mixed-file patch belong to Carry; an unrelated staged paragraph and uncertain draft do not. A's existing Carrier branch and target are established. The complete proposed parent Map includes authoritative markers, topology, Carry placeholders limited to branch, full base/baseline SHAs and immutable file links, plus a Start the Next Ticket protocol. The handoff must be accessible to a remote executor, and an eligible planning-created worktree was explicitly transferred for cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Delegate one bounded Carry and full Map publication, verify source disposition, and finish missing readiness in order.
assertions: scope-it leaves Scope/Ticket content checks, metadata and native publication with their sources; it sends the complete approved Map, parent destination, markers, allowed fill positions, existing binding and precise Carry/source/worktree evidence to to-afk-agent without rebuilding source artifacts.

to-afk-agent reuses A's Carrier branch, verifies exact carried diff, remote ref, full SHAs, immutable links, native linkage and executor access. It fills only the allowed Map positions and publishes/reads back one unique authoritative parent comment; the full Map is not copied to children.

Only after verified remote preservation and Map readback does to-afk-agent clean the unchanged selected source layers and eligible transferred worktree, preserving unrelated and uncertain content. It retains existing ready on A and adds/reads back missing ready on B after its preparation is complete. Because A was already ready and may be picked up automatically, it coordinates with the receiving workflow before changing A's executor inputs and reports any unresolved race.

An affected child lacking discovery context may receive only a concise canonical Map link and required execution pointers in an ordinary comment, without changing its Ticket body or native relationships. No dispatch, claim, implementation or PR starts.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it --publish after to-afk-agent created the full canonical Map comment on the parent but lost the create response. Scope/Tickets and Carry are verified. The supplied Map has identity markers, complete content and permitted verified substitutions; no comment ID was recorded. Variant A finds one exact matching parent comment; variant B finds two candidates; variant C finds no complete match but lookup was incomplete. A later ordinary parent comment exists in all variants.
evals.expected_output: Recover the one authoritative Map identity when provable, without duplicate creation or readiness on ambiguity.
assertions: Passes the supplied complete Map, markers, parent destination and permitted substitutions to to-afk-agent; a unique complete match is read back and bound by actual ID/URL, regardless of later ordinary comments.

Multiple candidates or incomplete lookup leaves publication identity unresolved and prevents retry, cleanup and new ready; recency, equivalent fragments and a lost response do not choose a canonical comment.
After unique recovery, resumes only unfinished source disposition and missing ready; preserves source artifacts, Map bytes and existing ready, and creates no duplicate comment or completion receipt.

evals.prompt: A planned amendment changes the Carry link and one Map field on a parent whose child Tickets already have ready-for-agent. Automatic pickup may occur. An executor has not been proven idle, and an earlier comment claims pickup is paused. The new file version and exact Map edit are approved but not yet applied. Another child has no ready yet. The parent Map's existing comment ID and editable markers are known.
evals.expected_output: Coordinate live pickup before changing executor inputs and preserve the authoritative Map identity.
assertions: Checks live claim/execution progress and coordinates with the receiving workflow before mutating inputs under existing ready; a comment does not suspend dispatch, and unresolved pickup race is reported without claiming the queue paused.

For a safe unclaimed case, to-afk-agent verifies replacement artifact access, edits only the approved Map boundary at the existing comment ID, reads back the full Map and preserved surrounding content, then completes source disposition before adding the other child's missing ready.

For an active claim or unresolved race, preserves existing ready and published inputs, does not silently change the executor's branch or Map, and seeks only the required coordination or changed-scope decision.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it in preview-only mode with reviewed Scope/Tickets drafts, selected Carry and a proposed full Map. The chosen tracker cannot publish a parent comment, and to-afk-agent cannot be resolved through the host in this run. An existing local Markdown fallback draft is available under the placement contract; no external writes or cleanup are approved. A source requires publication before it can finish its native review in a separate variant.
evals.expected_output: Provide a truthful local draft and gap report without claiming an AFK handoff.
assertions: Preview performs zero source, Git, Issue, Map, source-cleanup, worktree or ready writes; it may show complete proposed content, destinations and unresolved access/capability gaps.
The approved local fallback may retain a draft with accurate local bindings, but neither that draft nor an unavailable to-afk-agent counts as verified remote publication or completed AFK preparation.
The source-review variant pauses before treating its draft as complete; scope-it does not substitute its own review or silently invoke another source.

evals.prompt: Scope/Tickets and complete Map content are settled under scope-it --publish. Compare source disposition variants for the same Carry files: A gives no source preference; B explicitly says Retain local source; C resumes a legacy recorded Move; D resumes a legacy unanswered retain-or-move question. Remote preservation and Map publication are verified. One selected Ticket already has ready and permits automatic pickup; another lacks ready. The already-ready Ticket still needs a canonical Map link for discovery. A fresh receiving-workflow coordination check can establish a safe update window. In A/C, one selected untracked file is unchanged, one mixed tracked file has an unrelated staged hunk, and another selected source changed after capture. A planning-created worktree was explicitly transferred, while a pre-existing worktree is untouched.
evals.expected_output: Apply the correct source disposition and safe cleanup boundary without widening ownership.
assertions: to-afk-agent applies Clean up local source by default in A, explicit Retain in B, recorded Move in C, and requests resolution of the still-unanswered legacy choice in D; it does not retroactively apply the new default to D.

For A/C it removes only the wholly owned unchanged untracked file and selected unchanged layers of the mixed file, preserving unrelated staging and bytes. It retains the changed source and reports incomplete cleanup rather than inferring a replacement patch or declaring preparation complete.

For B it verifies unchanged retained sources and treats retention as complete when remote publication is verified. Eligible explicitly transferred worktree cleanup is assessed separately from source retention; the pre-existing worktree remains untouched.
Missing cleanup or disposition prevents newly adding ready; existing ready markers remain and any automatic pickup is coordinated without a claim that the queue is paused.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Start the Next Ticket protocol for a complete parent Delivery Map that to-afk-agent will publish before source cleanup and new ready markers. Later a session has only that Map and the parent. Children are ordered A then B, both open, unblocked and reliably unclaimed, but only B currently has the repository's ready marker. The task's Continue override prefers A when eligible. In a second variant the user names A without authorizing execution before its handoff finishes; in a third, B loses ready just before work. Cover the same preparation window for one Ticket represented by the parent and its Ticket comment.
evals.expected_output: Embed a durable protocol that checks live readiness for automatic selection and again before work, while handling named and single Tickets truthfully.
assertions: The published protocol itself requires the repository's live ready marker for autonomous pickup; neither the Map's existence nor an open, unblocked and unclaimed Ticket substitutes for readiness. It skips the ineligible Continue override A and selects B without loading every Ticket body.

For user-named A it surfaces missing readiness and requires separate execution authority before work; for a single Ticket it checks readiness on the parent identity and loads the Ticket comment only as selected context.

It re-reads readiness and native relations before work, so B losing ready prevents autonomous claim or implementation and produces a live no-eligible-Ticket report. It does not add ready or repair the unfinished handoff from the receiving session.
